requirements_source.access: Text taken from the Drive snapshot kept in evaluation-projects/docchange/docchange/drive_snapshot/03_RAG_Requirements_v1.md (a real Drive export). The v2_MOCK file in the same folder is an invented test revision and was not used.

repository.base_branch_note: The project's own git repository (prompt-c-rag/) has one commit on branch feature/rag-system and no remote. No starter baseline commit exists.
repository.import_method: Supplied project folder (and a .zip of it). The web interface in web_demo/ was added next to it by this integration; the project's own repository and source files were not modified.
repository.framework: Python standard library only. Project: command-line app (rag_app). Added by this integration: a stdlib HTTP server with a single-page web interface (web_demo/).
repository.backend: Python 3.12. BM25 keyword retrieval with stemming and synonyms (rag_app/retrieve.py); version resolution and chunking (rag_app/ingest.py); extractive answers with citations and abstention (rag_app/answer.py); optional OpenAI-compatible LLM rephrasing.
repository.routes: CLI: python -m rag_app --question/--demo/--interactive/--json/--kb/--llm. Web (port 8008): / and /api/health, /api/config, /api/examples, /api/documents (list, upload, remove), /api/ask, /api/reset.

tools.name: Python standard library
tools.reason: The project has no third-party dependencies, so it runs anywhere Python 3.9+ runs. The web layer follows the same rule (http.server, json).

tools.name: BM25 + stemming + synonyms (own implementation)
tools.reason: Transparent, deterministic and enough for a five-document knowledge base. An IDF-weighted key-term coverage check decides when to abstain.

tools.name: Extractive answering
tools.reason: Every answer sentence is copied from a document, so the default path cannot invent facts.

tools.name: OpenAI-compatible LLM (optional)
tools.reason: May rephrase from retrieved evidence only; output that cites an unknown file is rejected. Needs OPENAI_API_KEY or RAG_LLM_BASE_URL. Tested with fake transports; never run against a live model in this environment.

tools.name: Embeddings / vector database
tools.reason: Not needed for five short documents; the requirements allow simple local retrieval. The interface says so explicitly.

tools.name: Live Google Drive sync
tools.reason: The README states live Drive sync is not implemented; point --kb at a fresh export instead.

tools.name: Playwright + Microsoft Edge
tools.reason: Used to take the screenshot and to check the dashboard integration; not a dependency of the app.

limitations: Wrong answer on a near-miss: asked 'What is the international hotel reimbursement limit?', the system answers with the DOMESTIC limit (JPY 15,000) as if it applied. The old Prompt C abstained correctly. Retrieval does not treat 'international' versus 'domestic' as a qualifier that must match.

Safe miss on a paraphrase: 'when is the cutoff for expense claims?' is answered 'not found' although the document states the deadline; the old Prompt C answered it. The failure is safe (no invented fact) but unhelpful.
No embeddings or vector database: retrieval is keyword-based, so questions that share no words with the documents are not found.

The optional LLM rephrasing has only been run against fake transports, never a live model. Without OPENAI_API_KEY or RAG_LLM_BASE_URL the web interface reports that clearly and uses the extractive answer.
Live Google Drive sync is not implemented; the knowledge base is a folder export.
Uploaded documents exist only in a temporary folder and disappear when the server restarts.
No original snapshot of the project was supplied, and its repository has no remote. Its working tree shows deleted, previously committed .pyc files.
